nodes.description: Public uint256 state variable test1; declared in NFGasNames, never read or written by contract logic.
Public bytes32 state variable test2; declared in NFGasNames, never read or written by contract logic.
Public mapping(uint256 => string) names; persistent storage of name strings keyed by token id, written in setName.
Public IERC721 nfgas; reference to the external NFT contract whose ownerOf(id) is queried for access control.
Constructor(address a) that casts the supplied address to IERC721 and stores it in the nfgas state variable.
Public setName(uint256 id, string memory name): verifies NFT ownership, verifies that the name hash modulo 1025 equals id, then stores names[id] = name.
Caller-controlled address; used as the ownership requirement (nfgas.ownerOf(id) == msg.sender) gating the names[id] write.
Address parameter a of the constructor; used to instantiate the IERC721 nfgas reference.
Caller-supplied uint256 id parameter of setName; used as the ownerOf lookup key, the hash comparison target, and the names mapping key.
Caller-supplied string name parameter of setName; hashed with keccak256 for the id check and written into the names mapping.
Local variable hashValue = uint(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(name))) % 1025; compared against the id parameter in a require.
External call nfgas.ownerOf(id) on an attacker-influenceable ERC721 address, executed before any state update in setName.
State write names[id] = name executed after the external ownerOf call; mutates persistent storage based on validated caller input.

edges.reason: Constructor converts the supplied address into an IERC721 and assigns it to the nfgas state variable.
Constructor parameter a is consumed by the constructor body when building the IERC721 reference.
The address parameter a propagates into the nfgas state variable, fixing which external NFT contract will be called.
The nfgas state variable supplies the external contract target for the ownerOf(id) call inside setName.
The id parameter is passed as the argument of the external ownerOf(id) call.
msg.sender is compared with the return value of nfgas.ownerOf(id); this ownership check is the sole access-control gate for the function.
The names[id] state write can only be reached when msg.sender satisfies the ownerOf(id) ownership requirement.
The id parameter is used as the storage key of the names[id] = name assignment.
The name parameter is stored as the value of the names[id] = name assignment.
The name parameter is hashed with keccak256(abi.encodePacked(name)) to compute the local hashValue.
The require(hashValue == id) comparison ties the id parameter to the locally computed hashValue and reverts on mismatch.
Function setName computes and uses the local hashValue during its hash-validation step.
The hashValue check result controls whether execution of setName proceeds to the storage write.
setName performs an external call to nfgas.ownerOf(id); because nfgas is a caller-supplied contract address, the call can transfer control to untrusted code.
Function setName performs the names[id] = name storage write as its final action.
The external nfgas.ownerOf(id) call is executed before the names[id] = name state write, allowing a malicious nfgas contract to reenter setName and observe or mutate state mid-execution.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter a has no independent identity; its only role is to initialize the nfgas state variable, so it is folded into the constructor core node.
The id parameter is used solely as the key of the names[id] = name storage write, so it is merged into that unsafe operation.
The name parameter is stored directly into the names mapping by the names[id] = name write, so it is merged into that unsafe operation.
The local hashValue exists only inside setName to run the hash-validation require, so it is merged into the enclosing core function.
